newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks shake off weak Dow, end up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks shake off weak Dow, end up.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2376 +10.0 US 30yrcl 6.99 +0.03
10yrbond futs 91.865 -0.095 Gold NY 352.05 Lon fix 349.10
*Stocks shake off weak Dow, end slightly firmer on BHP strength, News bounce. Vol 325.65 million, value A$832.12 million, 1,090 stocks traded, 336 steady, 376 up, 378 down.

Australian stocks shook off a weaker Dow on Thursday, closing up slightly as firmer commodity prices helped a stronger resources sector overwhelm a bond market-led selloff in National Australia Bank Ltd.
But brokers said many investors remained on the sidelines in fear of what U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan might say in his congressional testimony starting at 1000 GMT on Thursday.
The All Ordinaries index closed up 6.1 points at 2,391 on reasonable turnover of A$832 million. The Broken Hill Pty Co's 24 cent rise to A$17.13 was the key driver.

NAB, seen the most vulnerable to weaker bond markets, closed down 20 cents at A$15.60 after local bond yields rose 10 basis points to 8.10 percent on fears that Greenspan would talk again about the possibility of a pre-emptive tightening.
"The market's really sitting on its hands, waiting for Greenspan to talk and to see what the Fed does next week," Morgan Stockbroking equities advisor Tony Russell said.

Brokers said firmer metals prices overnight and a reassessment of BHP's recent sharp selloff had helped boost the giant resources group's price. WMC Ltd also benefitted, closing up seven cents at A$8.16.
Some brokers said there appeared to be some switching out of RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd shares, which closed down three cents at A$18.42, into BHP.
"There's been a few broker upgrades on BHP too ahead of this quarterly result," said one Sydney dealer.
BHP is due to report its third quarter profit results on Friday.
Brokers also said Australian and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd appeared to benefit from a series of analysts briefings currently being conducted in Australia.
ANZ closed up 16 cents at A$7.88.
Mayne Nickless Ltd rose on renewed speculation of a resolution to the legal standoff between Seven Network Ltd and Optus Communications that is delaying the sale of Mayne's Optus stake.
Mayne closed up 21 cents at A$7.98, while Seven closed up five cents at A$4.40.
Brokers generally said a realisation that Australian stocks, and some in particular, had become oversold over the last month and the market had become short underpinned the strength.
"The market was so short that it had to have a bit of a bounce," said another Sydney dealer.

In other local markets, the 10-year benchmark bond yield spiked through 8.0 percent and to its highest level since October last year as futures attracted hedge fund selling. The 10 year bond futures closed down 0.105 at 91.885.

Comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane that he expected underlying inflation to remain close to the current level of 2.1 percent for the foreseeable futures had limited impact in a market already predicting a fairly benign outlook.
The Australian dollar edged a touch firmer to end at US$0.7875/85 in quite trade killed by a holiday in Japan.
